Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
652 AM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 258 AM EDT Wednesday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 258 AM EDT Wednesday...

1. Quiet weather today followed by showers and thunderstorms 
possible both Thursday and Friday. 

2. Following a drier weekend, shower chances return into early 
next week, with slightly above normal temperature.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 258 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure cresting overhead this 
morning will provide the region with a seasonable and dry day 
with partly sunny skies. Clouds will increase tonight ahead of 
next approaching system. A surface low pressure system will 
track from the Great Lakes area northeastward into Ontario and 
then Quebec. Series of frontal passages on Thursday into 
Thursday night will bring chances for showers and thunderstorms 
to our area. SPC has placed our region in Marginal risk for 
severe thunderstorms on Thursday. Moderate instability is 
expected ahead of a cold frontal passage as some higher 
dewpoints advect into our area on south southwesterly flow. Some
modest shear may help some storms to become better organized 
with some strong winds and small hail possible. Areas further 
south of our forecast area will have better chances for severe 
storms. Additional showers are expected Friday as upper level 
trough trails behind departing surface fronts and crosses our 
area. Severe weather is not expected, though embedded 
thunderstorms will be possible.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Following a mainly dry weekend, there still 
looks to be some signs of subtle cyclonic flow as an upper low 
lifts north and east, which may spur some isolated shower 
activity in eastern Ontario and southern Quebec late Sunday. 
Some of which will bring some increase cloud cover and an 
isolated shower to the St. Lawrence Valley and areas near the 
International Border. Our flow pattern will gradually become 
more zonal towards late Sunday into Monday, favoring more hit or
miss showers in the aforementioned areas. Temperatures will 
begin to increase above seasonable norms by 3-5 degrees, Sunday 
into Monday as a thermal ridge moves through the region. Highs 
Sunday into early next week will be in the upper 70s for the 
higher terrain, and low 80s in the wider valleys, which is 
supported by 850mb temperatures of 16-19C. Humidity will also be
on the incline, peaking Monday in the low to mid 60s. The 
increase in humidity will be a result of a trough swinging 
through the area to start next week. Models are beginning to 
pick up on a weak shortwave that will ride through the thermal 
ridge Monday into Tuesday. Shower chances will increase by early
Monday through Tuesday across the region. While ingredients 
will be marginal Monday, some thunder chances will be possible 
Monday afternoon driven by a weak frontal boundary passage. 
Thunder chances will also be possible Tuesday, but will be 
conditional on the frontal passage on Monday. A slower front 
Monday would help spur thunder chances, and perhaps some 
stronger storms Tuesday as storm chances would be associated 
with better instability and shear profiles. A faster front 
Monday would lower thunder chances Tuesday. While the pattern is
relatively unsettled early next week, precipitation 
probabilities are generally low, with only a 20-40% chance for 
0.5" highlighted in the northern portions of our area Monday 
into Tuesday in the GFS ensembles and AI suite.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 12Z Thursday...Fog and low stratus resulting in IFR vsbys and
cigs below 500ft agl at SLK/MPV/RUT is expected to improve towards
VFR between 12-13Z. Elsewhere low stratus to 3000-4000ft agl will
become more scattered this morning lifting to around 5000ft agl by
this afternoon. All sites should see VFR conditions beyond 14Z
through the daylight hours. Winds will generally be light and
variable 10 knots or less. A lake breeze at PBG/BTV will lead to
southeasterly and southwesterly winds, respectively, between 15 and
22Z. By tonight, winds will begin to shift to prevailing
southeasterlies and increase to prevailing 5-10 knots. There is a
chance for fog tonight across eastern Vermont, with some clearing
possible, though with winds above calm, there is low confidence at
any site.

Outlook...

Thursday: VFR. Likely SHRA, Chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
